## generic_waypoint_route_gen1

**Classification: reproduced dead-context shortcut.**

Audited generator SHA-256:
`b0c6b063ee8f18c10ddaefc8692939d88365692671eb8d255e0ced0b596cc3bc`.

Both the embedded rule program and Python oracle extract only the panel after
the final full-height separator. Earlier panels are presented as a nested route
sequence, but they do not influence the label. The task validator checks the
last panel's structure and broad sequence geometry without requiring earlier
panels to carry their claimed route state.

### Exact reproducible probe

`checks/audit/generic_waypoint_route_gen1/dead_context_probe.py` generated the
seed-23 medium task, then erased every nonseparator, nonbackground cell in every
panel before the last one. Across all four pairs, this removed 9–16 colored cells
per pair while preserving every output exactly. The tampered task still returned
`self_check_task == []`.

The complete source-bound report is
`checks/audit/generic_waypoint_route_gen1/dead-context-report.json`; its concise
execution log is `dead-context-probe.log`. The report includes original and
tampered input hashes, separator columns, last-panel offsets, the tampered task,
and the unchanged outputs.

Thus the exact shortcut “ignore every panel before the last full-height
separator” fits all generated labels. This is stronger than merely saying that
some historical context is redundant: the entire pre-final sequence is
erasable under the current checker.

### Additional check status

The optional selected task-test stage found no task-local or selected frozen
tests and exited non-passing with pytest code 5; see
`checks/audit/generic_waypoint_route_gen1/task-tests/result.json`. Recommended
repair: either make the output depend on the transition/history across panels,
or simplify the task to a single final panel and stop claiming nested-sequence
reasoning. If the sequence is retained, add a mutation test that erases or
permutes prior panels and require the label or validator verdict to change.

reasoning; add a mutation test requiring prior-panel erasure/permutation to alter the
